learning_outcomes.text: The students are able to explain the functionality of different CMOS devices and bipolar junction transistors in various electronic circuits.
The students are able to explain how basic analog circuits function and where they are applied.
The students are able to explain the functionality of fundamental operational amplifier circuits and their parameters.
The students are able to identify fundamental digital logic circuits and can discuss their advantages and disadvantages.
The students are able to name different memory technologies, to explain their functionality and architecture and to identify their parameters.
The students can calculate parameters of various CMOS devices and assess the fundamental effects of semiconductor physics that impact circuit design.
The students are able to analyze simple circuits with active components such as transistors, diodes, or operational amplifiers.
The students are able to dimension simple analog circuits with regard to design goals.
The students are able to analyze, design, and dimension digital circuits in different technologies.
The students are able work efficiently in heterogeneous teams.
The students can solve problems and answer professional questions when working together in small groups.
The students are able to assess their own learning progress and independently manage their learning processes.
The students are able to obtain the necessary information from the provided material and additional literature sources and they are able to put it into the context of the course.
